title: Mirror residual quantization
hypothesis: On a four-role matrix family generated by a shared base and a shared residual in a known Givens orbit, quantizing one shared residual and storing role coefficients plus charged Mirror coordinates will approach independent int4 activation error at materially lower serialized payload size than independent int4, while improving over residual-free Mirror.
physical_object: One symmetric int4 base matrix and one symmetric int4 shared residual matrix
mirror_coordinate: Four float32 Givens angles and four float32 residual coefficients, all charged
targeted_literature: PRQuant (identified by title in targeted search; URL/identifier not captured in search record)
controls: Mirror base plus private per-role int4 residual
Mirror base plus private per-role rank-2 residual
independent per-role int4 plus rank-2 QER residual

development.selection_metric: held-out Gaussian activation-output MSE and relative Frobenius error; fixed quantizer and rank; no optimizer updates or tuning

storage.authority: exact custom serialized inference payload bytes; every payload is deserialized and checked

success_gate: Both development worlds and all three fresh aligned worlds: Mirror shared-residual activation MSE <=1.10x independent int4 and payload <=0.65x independent int4; shared-residual Mirror also has at least 20% lower activation MSE than residual-free Mirror. Report independent teacher and low-rank control boundaries.
failure_gate: Both development worlds miss either the 1.10x independent-int4 quality ratio or the 0.65x actual-byte ratio. Keep fresh seeds sealed if the development gate fails.
boundaries: Aligned teacher is generated by the same Givens orbit and shared residual family
Independent arbitrary role matrices are a misspecification diagnostic
Fixed symmetric int4 and fixed rank-2 residual; no optimizer updates
No language-model quality or general compression claim
